strengths: Novel challenge to foundational ReLU-era assumptions in interpretability research; effectively demonstrates that negative pre-activations carry mechanistically important signal in modern smooth-activation LLMs

Excellent experimental methodology with well-designed sign-specific ablations and multiple appropriate controls (random, perplexity-matched) that isolate the specific contribution of Wasserstein neurons

Comprehensive multi-scale analysis spanning model-level, layer-level, neuron-level, and token-level perspectives, with particularly insightful layerwise analysis revealing early-layer origins and cumulative error patterns
Thorough empirical validation across 4 major model families (Pythia 70M-12B, Llama 3.1 8B, Mistral 7B, Qwen3 8B) with replication of core findings
Strong localization of effects to syntactic scaffolding tokens (determiners, prepositions, auxiliaries) via POS analysis, combined with clear dissociation from content words
Training dynamics analysis using publicly released Pythia checkpoints showing rapid emergence of Wasserstein neurons (~25K steps) that correlates with grammatical acquisition
Clear presentation with effective figures that communicate findings efficiently, complemented by logical narrative progression from motivation to mechanism to validation
weaknesses: Limited novelty beyond Sawmya et al. (2025) on Wasserstein neurons; contribution is primarily the application to syntax rather than discovery of the phenomenon itself

Insufficient theoretical grounding for why entangled neurons should preferentially use negative space for syntactic differentiation or why negative-negative separation is mechanistically superior to positive-negative
Narrow scope limits generalizability: syntax-only evaluation, English-only testing, and unclear whether negative pre-activation mechanism extends to semantic reasoning or other domains

Causality claims require strengthening: ablations show performance degradation but don't directly prove negative pre-activations implement syntax-specific computation vs. general capacity reduction; information flow analysis or integrated gradients would strengthen mechanistic claims
Arbitrary experimental choices with limited robustness analysis: top 1% WD threshold, model-specific perplexity-matched control percentages (20-50%), and MD/WD selection varying across sections

Statistical rigor concerns: overlapping error bars in multiple figures (6c, 6d, 7b, 7c), missing significance tests, moderate correlation coefficients without confidence intervals (e.g., R²=0.064 in 6d)

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: paper identifies that early layers are more critical but doesn't explain why; limited analysis of actual computations occurring in negative space vs. post-hoc observations

Limited practical impact: paper is fundamentally explanatory with no demonstrated applications to model improvement, pruning strategies, or architectural innovation; no code/artifacts for reproducibility mentioned
